messages:
incident-bot Alert: geo-dns-monitor detected inconsistent answers for api.redwood.example.com from multiple resolver vantage points :rotating_light:
alex_oncall: Getting paged. EU customers reporting 502/504s and long tails. Can folks triage DNS and origin health?
nina_sre: I'm oncall. Quick check: dig against 1.1.1.1 returns mixed A records across regions, some eu-west IPs, some us-east. Looks like geo routing is split-brain.
tom_net: Confirming. Cloudflare observed healthcheck flaps on eu-west origin pool starting ~10:12 UTC, but Route53 health checks are also showing transient failures. Could be a combination of instance NIC flapping in AZ-C plus negative caching at CF.
rachel_infra: Running dig and traceroute from several clouds:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.example.com @1.1.1.1
3.121.45.2
52.31.14.8
3.121.45.2
```
traceroute to 3.121.45.2 shows packet loss after eu edge hop.
priya_prod: Impact: Error budget for EU routes is being consumed; product alerting shows customer retries rising and a few partner integrations failing. Support has two open P1 tickets.
support_bot: Created ticket INC-2028-112. Notified account teams for customers: AcmeCorp, EuroShop, Finly, DataCloud.
alex_oncall: Proposed mitigation options: 1) Pause geo-based routing and switch record to static eu-central pool; 2) Force Route53 failover to eu-central failover record; 3) Increase Route53 healthcheck sensitivity to avoid flip-flop (longer failure window). I think immediate action is to cut traffic away from eu-west. Thoughts?
nina_sre: Agreed. Do (2) for quick atomic change. I'll prepare change-batch. We also need to instruct Cloudflare to clear unhealthy origin marks if possible.
tom_net: I'll open CF support chat and ask to clear origin status and reduce negative caching for the domain while we stabilize.
rachel_infra: Change-batch being prepared. Example payload:
```
{ "Comment": "Fail traffic from eu-west to eu-central due to AZ instability", "Changes": [ { "Action": "UPSERT", "ResourceRecordSet": { "Name": "api.redwood.example.com.", "Type": "A", "SetIdentifier": "eu-central-failover", "Weight": 0, "TTL": 20, "ResourceRecords": [{"Value":"52.31.14.8"}] } } ]}
```
Note: using TTL=20 to speed convergence.
alex_oncall: Execute when ready. I'll coordinate with CF. Nina, if change fails to propagate quickly we may need to add a temporary CNAME alias in Cloudflare to point to eu-central LB.
nina_sre: Applying change now.
(typing)
support_bot: Customer notice queued: "We are experiencing degraded service in EU region. Traffic is being rerouted to fallback endpoints. Engineers are actively mitigating."
(eyes) reaction from support_bot
priya_prod: Please also update status page to mention fallback to eu-central and ETA for resolution. Customers appreciate transparency.
tom_net: Contacted CF support referencing ticket #INC-2028-112 and requested immediate review of origin health state and negative cache purge. CF responded: "We can purge cache and request origin recheck; TTLs and negative cache may cause up to 60s discrepancy."
rachel_infra: Post-change dig from 8.8.8.8:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.example.com @8.8.8.8
52.31.14.8
52.31.14.8
```
Looks like answers converged to eu-central.
alex_oncall: Metrics dashboard shows EU 5xxs dropping within 45s of change. Good. Remaining task: monitor for recurrence and check eu-west instance health.
nina_sre: I'm going to leave the Route53 failover in place and schedule a deeper infra investigation. If CF still reports origin down after we've remediated, we'll coordinate with them on origin-level diagnostics.
priya_prod: Update from support: one enterprise customer reporting small data-sync delays; flagged as P1 but currently routed to fallback so severity downgraded.
support_bot: Noted. Added follow-up tasks to the ticket: "reach out to AcmeCorp success manager with timeline and mitigation steps."
(thumbsup) reactions from alex_oncall
alex_oncall: Handoff: I'm handing the incident to night oncall @rachel_infra in 15 minutes. Key points for the handoff:
- What happened: GeoDNS returned inconsistent IP sets due to eu-west origin flaps + Route53 healthcheck churn; CF negative cache amplified split answers.
- What we did: Applied Route53 failover/UPSERT to route EU traffic to eu-central with low TTL, requested CF to purge origin health cache, notified customers and updated status page.
- Open actions: infra to root-cause AZ-C NIC instability, CF follow-up on negative caching behavior, consider longer-term fix: unify healthcheck window and implement an intermediate proxy to smooth origin flaps.
rachel_infra: Acknowledged. I'll keep monitoring and will escalate to cloud provider if eu-west instance health shows host-level NIC errors. Alerts set: EU 5xx > 2% or DNS mismatch count > 5 per minute.
incident-bot Incident severity set to SEV2. Next scheduled update in 30m.
(white_check_mark) reactions across channel
alex_oncall: Thanks team. Good quick work. Please add any relevant logs to the incident ticket and we'll produce a post-incident writeup tomorrow.

-- end of thread --
